summary:
EarthLens is an open-source environmental intelligence platform that transforms NASA Earth observation data into accessible, scientifically supported insights.

Addressing the “Be an Earth System Trend Detective!” challenge, EarthLens helps users discover environmental changes, understand their potential mechanisms, and evaluate the reliability of scientific evidence.

Our case study investigates a region of Kalimantan, Indonesia, from 2003 to 2024, using four NASA datasets: GPM IMERG, MERRA-2, GLDAS, and MODIS.

The platform combines interactive visualizations, temporal trend analysis, spatial reliability assessment, an Evidence Passport, and bilingual scientific explanations through EarthLens Insights.

Our analysis of 16,632 burned-area cell-month observations across 63 geographic cells reveals seasonal wildfire patterns, regional warming, and environmental associations.

EarthLens bridges the gap between complex scientific data and public understanding by making statistical significance, data quality, uncertainty, and scientific limitations transparent.

Our mission is to make Earth observation science understandable, accessible, and trustworthy.
details:
EarthLens — Environmental Intelligence Engine

1. Project Overview

EarthLens is an open-source environmental intelligence platform developed by Team Everything Everywhere for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Our project addresses the challenge “Be an Earth System Trend Detective!” by transforming complex Earth observation datasets into accessible, interactive, and scientifically supported environmental insights.

Rather than simply displaying environmental data, EarthLens helps users answer five fundamental questions:

  • What is changing?
  • Where is it changing?
  • How much has it changed?
  • Why might these changes be occurring?
  • How reliable is the scientific evidence?

2. How EarthLens Works

EarthLens combines environmental data exploration with scientific analysis and educational explanations.

Users can explore environmental variables, investigate temporal and geographic patterns, inspect statistical results, and understand potential environmental mechanisms.

Our platform integrates three fundamental scientific pillars:

Discover: Environmental trend analysis and interactive visualizations.

Verify: Statistical significance, spatial reliability, data quality, and scientific uncertainty.

Understand: Accessible scientific explanations supported by references and environmental research.

3. NASA Earth Observation Data

Our case study focuses on a rectangular study region in Kalimantan, Indonesia, covering 111–115.5°E and 3.5°S–0°.

The common analysis period extends from 2003 to 2024.

We integrated four NASA Earth observation datasets:

  • GPM IMERG — Precipitation.
  • MERRA-2 — Air temperature.
  • GLDAS — Soil moisture.
  • MODIS MCD64A1.061 — Burned area.

These datasets allow EarthLens to investigate environmental relationships involving climatic conditions, water availability, and fire activity.

4. Scientific Methodology

Our scientific analysis includes:

  • Monthly and annual environmental time series.
  • Temporal trend estimation using HAC regression and Sen’s slope.
  • Seasonal Spearman correlation analysis.
  • Environmental anomaly assessment.
  • Spatial consistency assessment.
  • Benjamini–Hochberg and Benjamini–Yekutieli multiple-testing corrections.
  • Satellite observation quality and coverage evaluation.

The spatial analysis includes 63 geographic grid cells and 16,632 monthly burned-area records spanning 22 years.

The scientific datasets, methodologies, results, and analysis code are documented in our public GitHub repository to support reproducibility and transparency.

5. Scientific Findings

Our Kalimantan case study revealed several important environmental patterns.

Regional warming

Air temperature increased by approximately 0.262°C per decade. The regional warming trend remained statistically significant after multiple-testing adjustment.

Wildfire seasonality

Approximately 97.25% of the detected burned area occurred between July and October during the study period.

Environmental relationships

Seasonal Spearman correlations revealed strong negative associations between:

  • Soil moisture and burned area: −0.939.
  • Precipitation and burned area: −0.935.

These findings are consistent with environmental mechanisms linking seasonal water availability and conditions favorable to fires. However, these associations do not establish causation.

Spatial reliability

Of the 63 geographic cells, 62 were eligible for statistical analysis.

  • 19 cells showed nominally significant burned-area trends.
  • Two remained significant after Benjamini–Hochberg correction.
  • None remained significant after the more conservative Benjamini–Yekutieli correction.

These results demonstrate why multiple-testing corrections and scientific uncertainty are essential when interpreting environmental trends.

6. Our Innovation

Evidence Passport

The Evidence Passport provides transparent scientific information about environmental findings, including data provenance, statistical significance, data quality, uncertainty, and methodological limitations.

Instead of presenting every detected trend as an established fact, EarthLens helps users evaluate the strength of the available evidence.

Spatial Reliability Engine

This module evaluates geographic patterns, spatial trend consistency, statistical significance, and satellite observation coverage.

It helps identify situations in which apparently meaningful geographic trends may be affected by limited observations or multiple statistical comparisons.

EarthLens Insights

EarthLens Insights provides interactive environmental explanations and a scientific glossary in English and Spanish.

The module explains possible environmental mechanisms while clearly distinguishing observed findings, scientific hypotheses, and established causal relationships.

Its statistical interpretation rules are deterministic, supporting consistent and reproducible explanations.

7. Data Quality and Scientific Limitations

EarthLens explicitly communicates the limitations of Earth observation data.

For example, valid regional satellite coverage during October 2015 was approximately 46.6%. In situations with insufficient coverage, a low detected burned area cannot automatically be interpreted as an absence of fires.

Our current case study is regional, and the spatial reliability analysis focuses on burned area.

EarthLens is an exploratory scientific platform, not a validated disaster forecasting or causal inference system.

8. Technology and Development

The project uses Python for reproducible scientific analysis, Google Earth Engine for geospatial data extraction, and browser-based web technologies for interactive exploration.

CSV, JSON, and GeoJSON formats support scientific data storage, visualization, and integration.

GitHub provides version control, scientific documentation, and open-source collaboration, while GitHub Pages supports public access to the web application.

The project integrates scientific research, statistical analysis, software development, user interface design, and educational communication.

9. Benefits and Future Impact

EarthLens aims to make Earth observation science more accessible to students, educators, researchers, and the general public.

Our platform promotes scientific literacy by helping users understand not only environmental changes, but also how reliable the evidence behind those changes is.

Future development opportunities include expanding the platform to additional geographic regions, incorporating more NASA datasets, and supporting broader environmental education and research applications.

Our long-term vision is to bridge the gap between Earth observation science and public understanding.

AI/SI Usage Disclosure

EarthLens Insights uses deterministic interpretation rules rather than unrestricted AI-generated scientific conclusions.

AI-assisted code and content are identified through the corresponding project documentation and metadata.
